draft.title: Effects of globalisation on Australia
card: Globalisation is the growing links between economies through trade, investment, finance and the movement of people and ideas. Australia is a very open economy, so it feels these links strongly.
Consumers can buy cheaper imports, and firms can sell to larger overseas markets. Foreign investment can bring in funds, technology and new jobs.
Industries that cannot compete with imports may shrink, and workers in them can lose jobs. Some of those workers may need new skills to find other work.
Australia is also exposed to global shocks, such as a financial crisis or a pandemic. A downturn overseas can cut demand for Australian exports and reduce investment here.
draft.remember: Globalisation can lower prices and widen markets, but it can also cost jobs and bring in shocks from overseas.

a.q: Which of these is a cost of globalisation for Australia?
opts: A downturn overseas reduces demand for exports
Households can buy cheaper imported clothing
Wine producers can sell to more overseas buyers
Foreign firms bring new technology into Australia
a.why: A downturn abroad can cut demand for Australian exports, which is exposure to a global shock. The other three are gains: cheaper goods, bigger markets and new technology.
a.clue: Three options are gains. Which one is a problem from links with other economies?

b.q: Cheaper imported shoes lead Mia's shoe factory in Ballarat to close, and 80 workers lose their jobs. What does this show about globalisation?
opts: It can help consumers while hurting some industries
It lowers prices and also raises employment overall
It harms consumers and workers in the same industry
It has no effect on industries that export goods
b.why: Cheaper imports help consumers, but the local factory could not compete and workers lost jobs. The second option is wrong because the card says job losses can occur in some industries, and this case shows jobs falling.
b.clue: Think about who gains from cheaper shoes and who loses.

a.best: A downturn overseas reduces demand for exports

b.best: It can help consumers while hurting some industries

problems.detail: Why (b) says the 'second option' is wrong because this case shows jobs falling. That reasoning fits 'It lowers prices and also raises employment overall', not the option listed second ('It has no effect on industries that export goods'). Because the option order is random, referring to an option by position is unreliable. The why should name the option it rebuts and also explain why the export option and the 'harms consumers' option are wrong.

The right option is the only one with qualifiers ('can', 'some'). The others are absolute claims ('no effect', 'overall', 'harms consumers'), so a test-wise student could pick it without knowing the idea.
